method: Simulated skylines from the CTX DTM (not real photos). Terrain beyond the visibility V is hidden for both the observed skyline and the candidates; directions whose highest visible point is in the outer 15% of V are not scored (dust fade, not a hill). Edge noise 0.15 and 0.30 deg. 5 sites x 4 truth positions (0-50 m off-grid), prior 1-2 km off, 61 x 61 / 100 m grid, heading unknown.
falseFixDefinitionM: error > max(300 m, 2 x claimed uncertainty)
reliableNote: reliableMinVisKm (fix claimed in >= 80% of cases AND no false fix, both noise levels) was set before the first run. It is null: even in clear air the self-check claims a fix in only 55-80% of cases, because its RMS limit (3 x edge noise) also rejects good matches when the true position is between grid nodes. The check is conservative: it says 'no fix' rather than give a wrong one.
appRule: Used by skyline/skyline.js: visibility >= noFalseFixMinVisKm -> dust-aware Horizon Match (may answer 'no fix'); below it, or when the self-check says no fix -> lost-in-dust mode. Chosen after the first run from the false-fix criterion alone (stated here so it is not mistaken for a pre-registered rule).
